[ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](.claude/reference/ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/ReferencedSpecSidebarScope.md) should list every spec file and compiled spec
file the harness reads during the task's run, however it reads it, not only
those it opens with its file tools.

A spec file is one in the spec location; a compiled spec file is one under
`.claude/reference`. A file is referenced when:
- the task's prompt imports from it, as now
- the harness reads, edits, or writes it with a file tool, as now
- a shell command reads it, such as cat, head, tail, sed, less, grep, rg, awk,
  or diff naming it, or a pattern or folder that takes it in, as far as the
  command shows
- a shell command edits or writes it, such as sed -i, a redirect (> or >>),
  tee, mv, or cp onto it
- a search tool (Grep or Glob) searches a folder or pattern that takes it in
  and its results name it
- a subagent the harness starts does any of the above

A file taken in only by a folder or pattern, without the results naming it,
is not listed. A command whose target can't be worked out is skipped rather
than guessed at. Relative paths are read from the project directory.

Each file is listed once, in the order first referenced, the prompt's imports
first. The pencil icon shows on a file edited or written in any of these ways.
A row a subagent referenced shows its row the same way, with "Read by a
subagent" in its tooltip.

# Referenced Spec Sidebar Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

A second sidebar, at the right of the message list, that lists the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of the spec the harness is working from.

### Shape

#### Description

A column like the [SidebarScope](../sidebar/SidebarScope.md), but along the right of the message list rather than the left of the body, with a thin line down its left edge. It is resized by dragging that left edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160, and keeps the width it was dragged to while the application runs. It runs the full height of the message list, above the chat input, which stays across the full width of prompt mode.

#### Showing

It is only there while a task is running: from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the message list's right edge, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. The message list takes the rest of the width, laid out anew only once the slide settles, as when a file's split opens.

#### Contents

A header reads "Referenced spec", with how many files are listed, muted, at its right. Beneath it, one row per spec file the task references, each listed once: first those its prompt imports from, then the rest in the order the harness first reads, edits, or writes them. Each row shows its file icon, then its path from the project directory, cut off with an ellipsis when the sidebar is too narrow, its full path in its tooltip.
A spec file is one in the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../../scope/project-locations/ProjectLocationsScope.md) says, or a reference file under `.claude/reference`, which stands for part of the spec. It is referenced when the task's prompt imports from it, its hidden anchor naming it, or when the harness reads, edits, or writes it as the task runs, a file's full path counting however long it is. A file referenced again isn't listed again. Files anywhere else are not listed.
A file the harness has edited or written, rather than only read or imported, shows a small pencil icon at the right of its row.
Clicking a row opens its file, as the [OpenFileScope](../../../scope/open-file/OpenFileScope.md) says. While no spec file is referenced yet, the list reads "No spec files referenced yet", muted. The list scrolls with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/ScrollbarScope.md) when it is taller than the sidebar.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.

I've updated both the spec and the code. The sidebar now lists every spec file and compiled spec file the run references, whether through file tools, shell commands, search results or subagents. The build is clean, clippy raises nothing in the changed files, and all 239 tests pass. I haven't tried it in the running app with a real harness.

I compared the plan drawn from your prompt with the plan drawn from the updated spec in one pass myself, without running separate agents. They agreed on everything except what "as far as the command shows" means for a folder or pattern given to a shell command. I settled that the same way as for Grep and Glob: such a file is listed only when the command's output names it.

**Spec** (`spec/ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/index.pi`)
- The Contents section now spells out your definitions: a spec file vs. a compiled spec file, the six ways a file counts as referenced, and the rule that a file taken in only by a folder or pattern needs the results to name it.
- It also covers: commands whose target can't be worked out are skipped, relative paths are read from the project directory, files are listed in first-referenced order with imports first, the pencil shows for any edit or write, and subagent rows get "Read by a subagent" in their tooltip.
- `piton build` succeeded and the compiled `ReferencedSpecSidebarScope.md` reads correctly.

**Code**
- **`src/harness.rs`:** the harness output parser now passes on each tool call's full input and its result text, including from subagents. It used to drop subagent events entirely; the reply still shows only the main agent's text and tool calls.
- **`src/shell_paths.rs`** (new) works out which files a shell command touches:
  - **Reading:** cat, head, tail, sed, less, grep, rg, awk, diff, find, git diff and similar.
  - **Editing or writing:** `sed -i`, `>` and `>>`, tee, and mv or cp onto a file.
  - **Folders and patterns:** these are listed only when the output names the file, e.g. `spec/a.pi:3:…` or `==> spec/a.pi <==`.
  - **Handled correctly:** quotes, pipes, `cd`, and heredocs (the text inside a heredoc isn't read as commands).
  - **Skipped:** any target built from a variable or a `$(…)` substitution.
- **`src/referenced_spec.rs`:** a new tracker records every file the run references, marking whether it was edited and whether a subagent referenced it. The sidebar filters that list down to spec and compiled spec files, and the tooltip adds the "Read by a subagent" line.
- **`src/prompt_mode.rs`:** each task now feeds its events to that tracker, and the existing sidebar UI test uses the new events.

One behaviour to be aware of: a shell command that reads a file is counted only if the file exists at that moment. That stops a grep pattern like `spec/a.pi` from being mistaken for a file. Write targets don't need to exist yet.

The spec and reference files are still untracked, and the other changed files already had uncommitted edits when I started. Nothing is committed.
